notes: FAKES, labelled: everything after the first section runs on a second Stack whose Runtime is started with lib/moderator-stand-in-preload.mjs: (1) the content moderator that refuses every upload says 'allowed', (2) a module-load hook lets the attachments.* tools through the model-declaration filter in dist/agentRuntime.js. The shipped Runtime has neither (see the two defects). Records, object storage, text extraction, the ls/grep/read tools, scoping, dispatch and the model are the product's own.

The model declined most traversal requests itself (3 tool calls reached the tools out of 12 turns): the Chat tools have no direct door, so tool-level traversal handling is measured by the component probe below.

The owner's own GET /v1/conversations/:id/assets/:assetId answers 404 for a ready pipeline asset: that route reads the older transcript-reference store, so it is not a door to pipeline files for anyone (cross-scope refusal there is trivial). The refusals that carry weight are the tool and attach checks above.
The model declined to run the ten-file catastrophic grep three times; the bounded behaviour over many files is measured by the component probe.

COMPONENT probe (dist/assets/files.js and matchers.js, in-memory repository and blobs, a pass-through moderator): not the product edge, not product UAT. It exists because the Chat tools have no direct door and the model declines hostile calls.

The Studio research worker's model declined to run the catastrophic grep, so the Studio grep tool itself was not exercised on the real path. It uses the same regexMatcher (assets/matchers.ts) as Chat's grep; that matcher is measured directly by the component probe.

defects.title: Chat's ls/grep/read attachment tools are never declared to the model on a Product conversation
defects.expected: Spec (Attachments): retrieval is Unix style in both APIs: ls, grep and paged read. index.ts registers attachments.ls/grep/read 'for every Run'.
defects.actual: chatToolsForRun() (src/agentRuntime.ts) keeps a server tool only if its runtime name starts with `hatch.`, is Skill, or is in allowedExternalTools. For a Product conversation allowedExternalTools is corpusExternalTools(corpus), which holds only Creator http_function/mcp_tool ids, so `attachments.ls|grep|read` are filtered out. Asked to call ls, the real-Runtime model has no such tool; it can only reach the refused local file_* tools and tells the user it cannot read the file.
defects.repro: Product conversation with any attachment: ask the model to call its ls tool; the run's tool calls hold none and the reply says there is no such tool.

defects.title: Chat attachments cannot work on the real Runtime: every upload is refused because no content moderator is configured
defects.expected: Spec (Attachments): upload first, reference by assetId; ls, grep and paged read answer from the file, for every client.
defects.actual: POST /v1/conversations/:id/assets?name=report.md with a 300 KB markdown document returns 503 unavailable: "Uploads are unavailable: no content moderator is configured on this server.". src/chat/openChatAssets.ts constructs the AssetPipeline with options.moderator ?? new UnavailableModerator() and src/index.ts never passes a moderator, so Chat has no path to a ready asset. (Studio's openProductAssets does read aliyunModeratorFromEnvironment.)
defects.repro: Start dist/index.js with a Runtime database, create a conversation, POST any bytes to /v1/conversations/:id/assets?name=a.txt.

defects.title: A whole-document summary of a long attachment is built from about 1% of its text; the middle is skipped
defects.expected: Spec (Attachments): grep and paged read answer a whole-document summary, so the answer reflects the document's beginning, middle and end.
defects.actual: A 261980-character markdown report was summarized in 3 fresh conversations; 1/3 answers named facts from all three parts. Each Run made 3 to 5 grep calls and 1 to 3 default-size reads (8,000 characters per page, 33 pages in the file) and covered about 1% of the text (see measurements.summary_trial_N.coverage); the answers describe the middle as 'repetitive logs' instead of reading it. The tool description tells the model to page until next_offset is null, but nothing makes it.
defects.repro: Upload a 260 KB markdown file with a distinct fact near the middle, ask for a six-line summary covering start, middle and end, and read the Run's grep/read calls.
